k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_bind.description: Flags a ClusterRole whose declared rules allow the verb(s) bind on roles or clusterroles in rbac.authorization.k8s.io (a '*' in apiGroups, resources or verbs also matches). Such a grant lets any bound subject bind arbitrary Roles/ClusterRoles to any subject, bypassing RBAC escalation prevention to grant permissions the holder does not itself have cluster-wide (or in any namespace it is bound to). Only declared rules are read; bindings, aggregation and resourceNames narrowing are not considered.
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_bind.pass_when: No rule combines a matching API group, resource (roles or clusterroles or '*') and verb (bind or '*').
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_bind.fail_when: At least one rule matches the API group, resource and verb (bind on roles or clusterroles), including via '*' wildcards.
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_bind.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results), e.g. reserved system:/eks: names or rbac-defaults bootstrap roles.

k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_pod_create.description: Flags a ClusterRole whose declared rules allow the verb(s) create on pods in the core API group '' (a '*' in apiGroups, resources or verbs also matches). Such a grant lets any bound subject create Pods, which lets the holder schedule a Pod that mounts any ServiceAccount token, hostPath or privileged context in the namespace and so escalate to that identity or the node cluster-wide (or in any namespace it is bound to). Only declared rules are read; bindings, aggregation and resourceNames narrowing are not considered.
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_pod_create.pass_when: No rule combines a matching API group, resource (pods or '*') and verb (create or '*').
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_pod_create.fail_when: At least one rule matches the API group, resource and verb (create on pods), including via '*' wildcards.
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_pod_create.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results), e.g. reserved system:/eks: names or rbac-defaults bootstrap roles.

k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_secret_read.description: Flags a ClusterRole whose declared rules allow the verb(s) get, list or watch on secrets in the core API group '' (a '*' in apiGroups, resources or verbs also matches). Such a grant lets any bound subject read Secret objects, exposing ServiceAccount tokens, TLS keys and application credentials stored in the scope cluster-wide (or in any namespace it is bound to). Only declared rules are read; bindings, aggregation and resourceNames narrowing are not considered.
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_secret_read.pass_when: No rule combines a matching API group, resource (secrets or '*') and verb (get, list or watch or '*').
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_secret_read.fail_when: At least one rule matches the API group, resource and verb (get, list or watch on secrets), including via '*' wildcards.
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_secret_read.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results), e.g. reserved system:/eks: names or rbac-defaults bootstrap roles.

k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_wildcard_resou.description: Flags a ClusterRole with any rule whose resources entry contains a '*' character (e.g. '*' or 'pods/*') or whose verbs list contains the literal '*'. Wildcard grants silently extend to every current and future resource or verb, including Secrets, exec and RBAC writes, making the ClusterRole far broader than reviewed. apiGroups wildcards alone are not flagged by this variant.
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_wildcard_resou.pass_when: Every rule lists explicit resources without '*' and explicit verbs without '*'.
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_wildcard_resou.fail_when: Any rule has a resource string containing '*' or a verbs entry equal to '*'.
k8s.claude.clusterrole.no_wildcard_resou.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.cluster_ad.description: Surfaces every ClusterRoleBinding whose roleRef.name is cluster-admin as a MANUAL review item listing its subjects; it never returns PASS or FAIL. cluster-admin grants unrestricted '*' on all resources cluster-wide, so each holder is effectively a cluster owner and must be individually justified.
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.cluster_ad.pass_when: Never PASS: a cluster-admin binding is always returned as MANUAL for owner justification.
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.cluster_ad.fail_when: Never FAIL automatically; roleRef.name == 'cluster-admin' yields MANUAL with the subject list.
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.cluster_ad.not_applicable_when: When the binding references any role other than cluster-admin, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results) (e.g. system: bootstrap bindings).

k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_c.description: Flags a ClusterRoleBinding that binds at least one non-system User or Group subject (system:authenticated/unauthenticated/serviceaccounts groups count as non-system) to a ClusterRole whose rules grant update or patch on certificatesigningrequests/approval (certificates.k8s.io). Human or broad-group holders of this permission can approve arbitrary CertificateSigningRequests and so mint client certificates for any user or group, including system:masters-equivalent identities. The referenced ClusterRole is looked up in the complete ClusterRole inventory; ServiceAccount subjects and RoleBinding paths are out of scope.
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_c.pass_when: The referenced ClusterRole has no rule matching the permission (or the ClusterRole is not present in the inventory).
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_c.fail_when: A non-system User/Group is bound and the referenced ClusterRole grants update or patch on certificatesigningrequests/approval (certificates.k8s.io), including through '*' wildcards.
k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_c.not_applicable_when: When the binding has no non-system User or Group subjects (only ServiceAccounts or reserved system: identities), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

Human or broad-group holders of this permission can reach the kubelet API through the API server proxy, which allows command execution in any Pod on the node and bypasses audit of exec. The referenced ClusterRole is looked up in the complete ClusterRole inventory; ServiceAccount subjects and RoleBinding paths are out of scope.

Human or broad-group holders of this permission can create a PersistentVolume backed by a hostPath or arbitrary storage and mount node or other tenants' data into a Pod. k8s.claude.clusterrolebinding.no_human_w.description: Flags a ClusterRoleBinding that binds at least one non-system User or Group subject (system:authenticated/unauthenticated/serviceaccounts groups count as non-system) to a ClusterRole whose rules grant create, update or delete on validatingwebhookconfigurations/mutatingwebhookconfigurations (admissionregistration.k8s.io). k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_client_.description: Flags a supplied kubelet configuration whose authentication block exists but authentication.x509.clientCAFile is unset or empty. Without a client CA the kubelet cannot verify x509 client certificates, so the API server's kubelet client identity cannot be authenticated and the kubelet API falls back to weaker or anonymous authentication.
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_client_.fail_when: authentication is present but x509.clientCAFile is missing or empty.
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_client_.not_applicable_when: When the configuration describes a component other than kubelet; a configuration without an authentication block is MANUAL.

k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_streami.description: Flags a supplied kubelet configuration whose streamingConnectionIdleTimeout is a Go duration where every numeric part is zero (e.g. '0' or '0s'). A zero timeout disables idle cut-off for exec/attach/port-forward streams, letting abandoned or hijacked interactive sessions stay open indefinitely and exhausting kubelet resources.
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_streami.pass_when: streamingConnectionIdleTimeout is a valid duration with a non-zero component (e.g. 4h0m0s).
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_streami.not_applicable_when: When the configuration is not for kubelet; an absent field is MANUAL.

k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_strong_.description: Flags a supplied kubelet configuration whose tlsCipherSuites list is empty or contains any suite outside the CIS strong set (six ECDHE AES-GCM/CHACHA20 suites plus TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128/256_GCM). Weak suites such as 3DES or CBC-SHA let a network attacker downgrade or decrypt kubelet API traffic that carries exec streams and Pod logs.
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_strong_.pass_when: tlsCipherSuites is non-empty and every entry is in the strong-cipher allow-list.
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_strong_.fail_when: tlsCipherSuites is empty or contains a suite not on the allow-list.
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_strong_.not_applicable_when: When the configuration is not for kubelet; an absent tlsCipherSuites field is MANUAL.

k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_tls_cer.description: Flags a supplied kubelet configuration that declares only one of tlsCertFile/tlsPrivateKeyFile while serverTLSBootstrap is not enabled. A half-configured serving certificate means the kubelet falls back to a self-signed certificate that clients cannot verify, enabling man-in-the-middle of kubelet API traffic.
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_tls_cer.pass_when: serverTLSBootstrap is true, or both tlsCertFile and tlsPrivateKeyFile are non-empty.
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_tls_cer.fail_when: Exactly one of tlsCertFile/tlsPrivateKeyFile is declared and serverTLSBootstrap is not true.
k8s.claude.configuration.kubelet_tls_cer.not_applicable_when: When the configuration is not for kubelet; neither file declared (and no bootstrap) is MANUAL.

k8s.claude.cronjob.dashboard_not_deploye.description: Flags a CronJob whose regular containers (spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.containers[]) use a Kubernetes Dashboard image (path segment kubernetes-dashboard or kubernetesui/) or whose labels app, apps, k8s-app or app.kubernetes.io/name equal 'kubernetes-dashboard'. The Dashboard is a web UI frequently exposed with a privileged ServiceAccount; running it in each Job Pod the CronJob spawns on schedule provides an attacker-reachable path to cluster-wide read/write.
k8s.claude.cronjob.dashboard_not_deploye.pass_when: No regular container image matches the Dashboard pattern and no inspected label equals kubernetes-dashboard.
k8s.claude.cronjob.dashboard_not_deploye.fail_when: Any regular container image matches (^|/)(kubernetes-dashboard|kubernetesui/) or a Dashboard label is present.
k8s.claude.cronjob.dashboard_not_deploye.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.cronjob.no_privileged_port.description: Flags a CronJob where any regular container in spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec declares a ports[].containerPort below 1024. Binding a privileged port requires root or CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE inside the container, so the declaration signals that each Job Pod the CronJob spawns on schedule needs elevated privileges that would otherwise be unnecessary.
k8s.claude.cronjob.no_privileged_port.pass_when: Every declared containerPort is 1024 or higher.
k8s.claude.cronjob.no_privileged_port.fail_when: Any regular container declares a containerPort below 1024.
k8s.claude.cronjob.no_privileged_port.not_applicable_when: When no regular container declares any ports, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.claude.cronjob.secrets_as_files.description: Flags a CronJob whose regular containers inject Secrets as environment variables, via env[].valueFrom.secretKeyRef or envFrom[].secretRef, in spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec. Environment-variable Secrets in each Job Pod the CronJob spawns on schedule leak through process listings, crash dumps, child processes and logging, and cannot be rotated without a restart, unlike mounted Secret volumes.
k8s.claude.cronjob.secrets_as_files.pass_when: No regular container references a Secret through env secretKeyRef or envFrom secretRef.
k8s.claude.cronjob.secrets_as_files.fail_when: At least one regular container uses env valueFrom.secretKeyRef or envFrom secretRef.
k8s.claude.cronjob.secrets_as_files.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); init and ephemeral containers are not inspected.

This file is the kubelet kubeconfig, which holds the node's API client credentials; group- or world-accessible modes let other local users read secrets or tamper with kubelet behaviour.

k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippet_alia.description: Flags an Ingress carrying a snippet annotation whose value contains 'alias', evaluated only when the collector marked the annotation projection complete. An alias directive in a snippet can map an HTTP location onto arbitrary controller filesystem paths, exposing the controller's mounted token and certificates over HTTP.
k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippet_alia.pass_when: No annotation matches the condition in a complete annotation projection.
k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippet_alia.fail_when: Ingress has a snippet annotation whose value contains 'alias'.
k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippet_alia.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); filtered annotations (annotations_complete != true) yield UNKNOWN.

k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippet_lua.description: Flags an Ingress carrying a snippet annotation whose value matches lua_, _lua or the literal 'kubernetes.io', evaluated only when the collector marked the annotation projection complete. Embedded Lua (content_by_lua_block etc.) executes arbitrary code inside the ingress-nginx controller process, giving cluster-wide Secret access.
k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippet_lua.pass_when: No annotation matches the condition in a complete annotation projection.
k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippet_lua.fail_when: Ingress has a snippet annotation whose value matches lua_, _lua or the literal 'kubernetes.io'.
k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippet_lua.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); filtered annotations (annotations_complete != true) yield UNKNOWN.

k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippets.description: Flags an Ingress carrying any annotation whose key contains 'snippet', evaluated only when the collector marked the annotation projection complete. Snippet annotations (server-snippet, configuration-snippet, auth-snippet) inject raw NGINX configuration into the shared ingress-nginx controller; anyone who can write an Ingress can then read the controller's ServiceAccount token and Secrets of all namespaces (CVE-2021-25742).

k8s.claude.ingress.no_nginx_snippets.fail_when: Ingress has any annotation whose key contains 'snippet'.

k8s.claude.job.no_privileged_port.description: Flags a Job where any regular container in spec.template.spec declares a ports[].containerPort below 1024. k8s.claude.pod.capabilities_dropped.description: Flags a Pod where a regular container declares a securityContext.capabilities block that either adds any capability or drops none. Declaring capabilities without dropping any keeps the full container-runtime default set (including NET_RAW, CHOWN, SETUID), widening the kernel attack surface for container escape.

k8s.claude.pod.controller_manager_gc_thr.description: Flags a kube-controller-manager static Pod declaration whose --terminated-pod-gc-threshold flag is 0 or the 12500 default. At the default, up to 12500 terminated Pods accumulate before garbage collection, bloating etcd and slowing the API server; 0 disables GC entirely.

k8s.claude.pod.etcd_unique_ca.description: Compares the etcd static Pod's --trusted-ca-file path with every kube-apiserver --client-ca-file path in the complete Pod inventory and FAILs when they are the same file. If etcd trusts the cluster client CA, any certificate issued for Kubernetes clients (including kubelets) can authenticate directly to etcd and read or rewrite all cluster state and Secrets. Differing paths are MANUAL because certificate contents are not compared.

k8s.claude.pod.etcd_unique_ca.fail_when: The etcd trusted-ca-file path equals a kube-apiserver client-ca-file path.
k8s.claude.pod.etcd_unique_ca.not_applicable_when: When the Pod is not an etcd declaration, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

For each Pod the Job launches, root containers turn any escape, writable mount or kernel bug into node root.
k8s.job.non_root.pass_when: Every container resolves to runAsNonRoot: true and no runAsUser of 0.
k8s.job.non_root.fail_when: Any container lacks runAsNonRoot: true or resolves to runAsUser 0.
k8s.job.non_root.not_applicable_when: When spec.template.spec.os.name is windows (Linux-only predicate), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.namespace.quota_limits_cpu.description: Flags a Namespace with no unscoped ResourceQuota whose spec.hard sets limits.cpu, using the complete ResourceQuota inventory. Without a namespace-wide cap on total CPU limits, one tenant or compromised workload can consume cluster capacity and starve other namespaces. A quota limited by scopes/scopeSelector only yields MANUAL.
k8s.namespace.quota_limits_cpu.pass_when: At least one ResourceQuota in the namespace without scopes/scopeSelector declares hard['limits.cpu'].
k8s.namespace.quota_limits_cpu.fail_when: No ResourceQuota in the namespace declares hard['limits.cpu'] at all.
k8s.namespace.quota_limits_cpu.not_applicable_when: When the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results) (kube-system, kube-public, kube-node-lease, provider namespaces); incomplete quota inventory is UNKNOWN.

k8s.namespace.quota_limits_memory.description: Flags a Namespace with no unscoped ResourceQuota whose spec.hard sets limits.memory, using the complete ResourceQuota inventory. Without a namespace-wide cap on total memory limits, one tenant or compromised workload can consume cluster capacity and starve other namespaces. A quota limited by scopes/scopeSelector only yields MANUAL.
k8s.namespace.quota_limits_memory.pass_when: At least one ResourceQuota in the namespace without scopes/scopeSelector declares hard['limits.memory'].

k8s.namespace.quota_requests_cpu.description: Flags a Namespace with no unscoped ResourceQuota whose spec.hard sets requests.cpu, using the complete ResourceQuota inventory. Without a namespace-wide cap on total CPU requests, one tenant or compromised workload can consume cluster capacity and starve other namespaces. A quota limited by scopes/scopeSelector only yields MANUAL.
k8s.namespace.quota_requests_cpu.pass_when: At least one ResourceQuota in the namespace without scopes/scopeSelector declares hard['requests.cpu'].

k8s.namespace.quota_requests_memory.description: Flags a Namespace with no unscoped ResourceQuota whose spec.hard sets requests.memory, using the complete ResourceQuota inventory. Without a namespace-wide cap on total memory requests, one tenant or compromised workload can consume cluster capacity and starve other namespaces. A quota limited by scopes/scopeSelector only yields MANUAL.
k8s.namespace.quota_requests_memory.pass_when: At least one ResourceQuota in the namespace without scopes/scopeSelector declares hard['requests.memory'].

k8s.namespace.restricted_admission.description: Flags a Namespace whose pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce label is set to privileged or baseline instead of restricted. Below restricted, Pod Security Admission admits Pods running as root, with added capabilities or without seccomp, so a namespace writer can deploy escape-prone workloads.
k8s.namespace.restricted_admission.fail_when: The enforce label is privileged or baseline.
k8s.namespace.restricted_admission.not_applicable_when: When the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); an absent enforce label (cluster defaults unknown) is UNKNOWN.

k8s.network.namespace_policy_inventory.description: Flags a Namespace that has zero NetworkPolicy objects in a complete NetworkPolicy inventory; if policies exist the result is MANUAL, never PASS. With no NetworkPolicy every Pod in the namespace accepts traffic from and sends traffic to any Pod in the cluster, enabling lateral movement after one compromise.
k8s.network.namespace_policy_inventory.pass_when: Never PASS automatically: one or more policies yields MANUAL coverage review.
k8s.network.namespace_policy_inventory.fail_when: The complete inventory contains no NetworkPolicy in the namespace.
k8s.network.namespace_policy_inventory.not_applicable_when: When the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); incomplete NetworkPolicy inventory is UNKNOWN.

k8s.pod.default_proc_mount.description: Flags a Pod where any container (regular, init or ephemeral) sets securityContext.procMount to Unmasked. An unmasked /proc exposes kernel interfaces (e.g. /proc/sys, /proc/kcore) normally hidden by the runtime, aiding information leaks and container escape.
k8s.pod.default_proc_mount.pass_when: All containers use procMount Default (or omit it).
k8s.pod.default_proc_mount.not_applicable_when: When spec.os.name is windows (Linux-only control), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results). Unknown procMount values are UNKNOWN.

k8s.pod.drop_capabilities.description: Flags a Pod where any container (regular, init or ephemeral) does not list the literal 'ALL' in securityContext.capabilities.drop. Without dropping ALL, the container keeps the runtime's default capability set (NET_RAW, SETUID, CHOWN, DAC_OVERRIDE...), widening the kernel privilege available to an attacker.
k8s.pod.drop_capabilities.not_applicable_when: When spec.os.name is windows (Linux-only control), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.pod.no_default_serviceaccount.description: Flags a Pod whose spec.serviceAccountName is omitted, empty or 'default'. Workloads sharing the namespace default ServiceAccount share its token and any RBAC granted to it, so one compromised Pod inherits permissions intended for others and access cannot be scoped per workload.
k8s.pod.no_default_serviceaccount.pass_when: serviceAccountName names a dedicated non-default ServiceAccount.
k8s.pod.no_default_serviceaccount.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.pod.no_host_namespaces.description: Flags a Pod that sets any of spec.hostNetwork, spec.hostPID or spec.hostIPC to true. Sharing any host namespace removes a core isolation boundary: host network exposes node traffic and local services, host PID allows process inspection/ptrace, host IPC exposes shared memory.
k8s.pod.no_host_namespaces.pass_when: All three flags are false or omitted.
k8s.pod.no_host_namespaces.fail_when: Any of hostNetwork, hostPID or hostIPC is true.
k8s.pod.no_host_namespaces.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.pod.no_host_ports.description: Flags a Pod where any container (regular, init or ephemeral) declares a non-zero ports[].hostPort. hostPort publishes the container on the node IP outside Service and NetworkPolicy control and can shadow node services.
k8s.pod.no_host_ports.pass_when: All hostPort values are 0 or omitted.
k8s.pod.no_host_ports.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.pod.no_hostpath.description: Flags a Pod whose spec.volumes includes any hostPath volume. hostPath mounts node directories into the container; paths like /, /etc, /var/lib/kubelet or the container runtime socket allow reading node credentials or full node takeover.
k8s.pod.no_hostpath.fail_when: At least one volume declares hostPath (reported with its path).
k8s.pod.no_hostpath.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.pod.no_privilege_escalation.description: Flags a Pod where any container (regular, init or ephemeral) does not explicitly set securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation: false (the API default is true). With escalation allowed, setuid binaries and file capabilities inside the image can raise the process above its starting privileges (no_new_privs is not set).
k8s.pod.no_privilege_escalation.fail_when: Any container omits it or sets it true.
k8s.pod.no_privilege_escalation.not_applicable_when: When spec.os.name is windows (Linux-only control), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.pod.no_privileged_containers.description: Flags a Pod where any container (regular, init or ephemeral) sets securityContext.privileged: true. Privileged containers receive all capabilities, device access and disabled confinement, making escape to the node trivial.
k8s.pod.no_privileged_containers.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.pod.non_root.description: Flags a Pod where any container (regular, init or ephemeral) neither resolves runAsNonRoot: true nor a positive runAsUser, or resolves runAsUser 0 (container value overriding Pod securityContext). Containers that may run as root turn any escape, writable host mount or kernel flaw into root on the node.
k8s.pod.non_root.pass_when: Every container resolves to runAsUser != 0 and either runAsNonRoot: true or runAsUser > 0.
k8s.pod.non_root.fail_when: Any container may run as root (no non-root declaration, or runAsUser 0).
k8s.pod.non_root.not_applicable_when: When spec.os.name is windows (Linux-only control), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.pod.read_only_root.description: Flags a Pod where any container (regular, init or ephemeral) does not set securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true. A writable root filesystem lets an attacker drop tools, modify binaries or persist inside the container.
k8s.pod.read_only_root.fail_when: Any container omits it or sets false.
k8s.pod.read_only_root.not_applicable_when: When spec.os.name is windows (Linux-only control), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.pod.restrict_added_capabilities.description: Flags a Pod where any container (regular, init or ephemeral) adds a capability other than NET_BIND_SERVICE in securityContext.capabilities.add, the Pod Security restricted allowance. Capabilities such as SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN or SYS_PTRACE provide kernel-level powers commonly abused for container escape.
k8s.pod.restrict_added_capabilities.pass_when: capabilities.add is empty or only NET_BIND_SERVICE for every container.
k8s.pod.restrict_added_capabilities.fail_when: Any container adds a capability other than NET_BIND_SERVICE.
k8s.pod.restrict_added_capabilities.not_applicable_when: When spec.os.name is windows (Linux-only control), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.pod.restrict_selinux_identity.description: Flags a Pod where the Pod-level or any container securityContext.seLinuxOptions sets a custom user or role. Overriding the SELinux user/role can place the process in a more privileged SELinux identity and defeat the MAC confinement the node policy relies on.
k8s.pod.restrict_selinux_identity.pass_when: No seLinuxOptions.user or .role is set anywhere.
k8s.pod.restrict_selinux_identity.fail_when: Pod or any container sets seLinuxOptions.user or .role.
k8s.pod.restrict_selinux_identity.not_applicable_when: When spec.os.name is windows (Linux-only control), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.pod.restrict_token_automount.description: Flags a Pod that explicitly sets spec.automountServiceAccountToken: true. A mounted API token is readable by any process in the Pod, so an application compromise yields Kubernetes API credentials for its ServiceAccount.
k8s.pod.restrict_token_automount.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); an omitted field (inherited from the ServiceAccount) is UNKNOWN.

k8s.pod.seccomp.description: Flags a Pod where any container (regular, init or ephemeral) resolves no seccompProfile.type of RuntimeDefault or Localhost (container value, else Pod value), i.e. Unconfined or unset. Without a seccomp filter the full syscall table is reachable, exposing kernel exploits to the workload.
k8s.pod.seccomp.pass_when: Every container resolves to RuntimeDefault or Localhost (with a localhostProfile).
k8s.pod.seccomp.fail_when: Any container resolves to Unconfined or no profile.
k8s.pod.seccomp.not_applicable_when: When spec.os.name is windows (Linux-only control), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.ports.clusterrole.cluster_role_with_.description: Flags a ClusterRole with a rule that literally lists apiGroup admissionregistration.k8s.io, resource validatingwebhookconfigurations or mutatingwebhookconfigurations, and verb create, update or patch. Webhook writers can register admission hooks that see and mutate every API request, e.g. injecting sidecars or exfiltrating Secrets at creation. Exact symbols only; '*' grants are left to the wildcard check.
k8s.ports.clusterrole.cluster_role_with_.pass_when: No rule literally combines that group, a webhook configuration resource and create/update/patch.
k8s.ports.clusterrole.cluster_role_with_.fail_when: A rule literally lists the group, a webhook configuration resource and create/update/patch.
k8s.ports.clusterrole.cluster_role_with_.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.ports.clusterrole.role_with_rbac_app.description: Flags a ClusterRole with a certificates.k8s.io rule granting update/patch on certificatesigningrequests/approval or the approve verb on signers (literal symbols). CSR approval lets the holder issue client certificates for arbitrary identities, including node or administrator groups, for persistent cluster access.
k8s.ports.clusterrole.role_with_rbac_app.pass_when: No rule grants CSR approval or signer approve.
k8s.ports.clusterrole.role_with_rbac_app.fail_when: A rule grants update/patch on certificatesigningrequests/approval or approve on signers.
k8s.ports.clusterrole.role_with_rbac_app.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.ports.clusterrole.role_with_rbac_esc.description: Flags a ClusterRole with an rbac.authorization.k8s.io rule granting the literal escalate verb on roles or clusterroles. escalate disables RBAC's privilege-escalation check, letting the holder edit roles to include permissions it does not possess, up to cluster-admin.
k8s.ports.clusterrole.role_with_rbac_esc.pass_when: No rule grants escalate on roles/clusterroles.
k8s.ports.clusterrole.role_with_rbac_esc.fail_when: A rule grants escalate on roles or clusterroles.
k8s.ports.clusterrole.role_with_rbac_esc.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.ports.clusterrole.role_with_wildcard.description: Flags a ClusterRole where any rule's apiGroups, resources or verbs contains a string with a '*' character. Wildcards in any of the three fields automatically extend the grant to new API groups, resources or verbs, producing over-privileged roles that are hard to audit.
k8s.ports.clusterrole.role_with_wildcard.pass_when: No rule contains '*' in apiGroups, resources or verbs.
k8s.ports.clusterrole.role_with_wildcard.fail_when: Any rule contains '*' in apiGroups, resources or verbs.
k8s.ports.clusterrole.role_with_wildcard.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

k8s.ports.clusterrolebinding.cluster_rol.description: Flags a ClusterRoleBinding with a subject of kind ServiceAccount named 'default' in any namespace. Every Pod that does not set serviceAccountName runs as that namespace's default ServiceAccount, so granting it cluster-wide permissions hands them to every such Pod.
k8s.ports.clusterrolebinding.cluster_rol.pass_when: No subject is a ServiceAccount named default.
k8s.ports.clusterrolebinding.cluster_rol.fail_when: At least one subject is ServiceAccount 'default'.
k8s.ports.clusterrolebinding.cluster_rol.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); a binding without a subjects field is UNKNOWN.

k8s.ports.configmap_metadata.config_map_.description: Flags a ConfigMap whose metadata.namespace is 'default'. Objects in the default namespace share it with ad-hoc and legacy workloads, so RBAC and NetworkPolicy boundaries are weak and configuration is exposed to anything granted default-namespace access.
k8s.ports.configmap_metadata.config_map_.pass_when: The ConfigMap lives in a namespace other than default.
k8s.ports.configmap_metadata.config_map_.not_applicable_when: When the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results) (e.g. the kube-root-ca.crt ConfigMap).

k8s.ports.configuration.kubelet_authoriz.description: Flags a supplied kubelet configuration whose authorization.mode is not 'Webhook'. With AlwaysAllow, any authenticated (or anonymous) caller of the kubelet API can exec into Pods and read logs without API-server RBAC.
k8s.ports.configuration.kubelet_authoriz.not_applicable_when: When the configuration describes a component other than kubelet, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); a missing field is UNKNOWN.

k8s.ports.configuration.kubelet_disable_.description: Flags a supplied kubelet configuration whose authentication.anonymous.enabled is not false. Anonymous kubelet authentication lets unauthenticated network callers reach the kubelet API on port 10250.
k8s.ports.configuration.kubelet_disable_.not_applicable_when: When the configuration describes a component other than kubelet, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); a missing field is UNKNOWN.

k8s.ports.configuration.kubelet_disable_.description: Flags a supplied kubelet configuration whose readOnlyPort is not 0. The read-only port (10255) serves unauthenticated Pod specs and node metrics that reveal workload details and environment.
k8s.ports.configuration.kubelet_disable_.not_applicable_when: When the configuration describes a component other than kubelet, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); a missing field is UNKNOWN.

k8s.ports.configuration.kubelet_manage_i.description: Flags a supplied kubelet configuration whose makeIPTablesUtilChains is not true. Without kubelet-managed iptables utility chains, network rules for Pods can drift from the kubelet's expectations, breaking traffic isolation.
k8s.ports.configuration.kubelet_manage_i.not_applicable_when: When the configuration describes a component other than kubelet, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); a missing field is UNKNOWN.

k8s.ports.configuration.kubelet_rotate_c.description: Flags a supplied kubelet configuration whose rotateCertificates is not true. Without client-certificate rotation the kubelet keeps using an expiring or compromised credential with no automatic replacement.
k8s.ports.configuration.kubelet_rotate_c.not_applicable_when: When the configuration describes a component other than kubelet, or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); a missing field is UNKNOWN.

k8s.ports.cronjob.always_pull.description: Flags a CronJob where any container (regular, init or ephemeral) would not pull on every start: imagePullPolicy is explicitly IfNotPresent/Never, or omitted on a tagged non-latest image; content-addressed sha256 digests with IfNotPresent/omitted/Always are accepted in its Pod template at spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec. For each Job Pod the CronJob spawns on schedule, cached images on the node can be reused by other tenants without registry authorization, and a node-cached poisoned image is trusted.
k8s.ports.cronjob.always_pull.pass_when: Every container uses Always, an untagged/latest image with no explicit policy, or a valid sha256 digest with policy unset/IfNotPresent/Always.
k8s.ports.cronjob.always_pull.fail_when: Any container has an empty image; any container uses Never, or a tagged image with IfNotPresent or no policy.
k8s.ports.cronjob.always_pull.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); malformed or missing PodSpec facts are UNKNOWN.

k8s.ports.cronjob.container_admission_co.description: Flags a CronJob whose Pod template (spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec) contains a container identified as kube-apiserver whose captured command-line flags show a failing value: FAIL when the --enable-admission-plugins list does not include AlwaysPullImages. Without AlwaysPullImages, Pods in a multi-tenant cluster can run private images already cached on the node without registry credentials. Only explicit flag declarations in the collected component projection are compared; config files and defaults are not inferred.
k8s.ports.cronjob.container_admission_co.pass_when: Every captured kube-apiserver container: the comma-separated --enable-admission-plugins list includes AlwaysPullImages.
k8s.ports.cronjob.container_admission_co.fail_when: Any captured kube-apiserver container: the --enable-admission-plugins list does not include AlwaysPullImages.
k8s.ports.cronjob.container_admission_co.not_applicable_when: When no container in the CronJob template is captured as kube-apiserver (component metadata), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); a flag omitted from the projection is UNKNOWN.

k8s.ports.cronjob.container_admission_co.description: Flags a CronJob whose Pod template (spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec) contains a container identified as kube-apiserver whose captured command-line flags show a failing value: FAIL when the --enable-admission-plugins list includes AlwaysAdmit. AlwaysAdmit accepts every request and neutralises all other admission control. Only explicit flag declarations in the collected component projection are compared; config files and defaults are not inferred.
k8s.ports.cronjob.container_admission_co.pass_when: Every captured kube-apiserver container: the --enable-admission-plugins list does not include AlwaysAdmit.
k8s.ports.cronjob.container_admission_co.fail_when: Any captured kube-apiserver container: the --enable-admission-plugins list includes AlwaysAdmit.
k8s.ports.cronjob.container_admission_co.not_applicable_when: When no container in the CronJob template is captured as kube-apiserver (component metadata), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); a flag omitted from the projection is UNKNOWN.

k8s.ports.cronjob.container_arg_peer_cli.description: Flags a CronJob whose Pod template (spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec) contains a container identified as etcd whose captured command-line flags show a failing value: FAIL when --peer-client-cert-auth is declared with a value other than 'true'. Without peer client-certificate authentication any host reaching the etcd peer port can join or read replication traffic. Only explicit flag declarations in the collected component projection are compared; config files and defaults are not inferred.
k8s.ports.cronjob.container_arg_peer_cli.fail_when: Any captured etcd container: --peer-client-cert-auth is declared with a value other than 'true'.
k8s.ports.cronjob.container_arg_peer_cli.not_applicable_when: When no container in the CronJob template is captured as etcd (component metadata), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); a flag omitted from the projection is UNKNOWN.

k8s.ports.cronjob.container_argument_ano.description: Flags a CronJob whose Pod template (spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec) contains a container identified as kubelet whose captured command-line flags show a failing value: FAIL when --anonymous-auth is declared with a value other than 'false'. Anonymous kubelet authentication lets unauthenticated callers reach the kubelet API (10250) for exec, logs and Pod listing. Only explicit flag declarations in the collected component projection are compared; config files and defaults are not inferred.
k8s.ports.cronjob.container_argument_ano.fail_when: Any captured kubelet container: --anonymous-auth is declared with a value other than 'false'.
k8s.ports.cronjob.container_argument_ano.not_applicable_when: When no container in the CronJob template is captured as kubelet (component metadata), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); a flag omitted from the projection is UNKNOWN.

k8s.ports.cronjob.container_argument_api.description: Flags a CronJob whose Pod template (spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec) contains a container identified as kube-apiserver whose captured command-line flags show a failing value: FAIL when --anonymous-auth is declared with a value other than 'false'. Anonymous API server requests are mapped to system:anonymous, so any RBAC accidentally granted to it or system:unauthenticated becomes unauthenticated access. Only explicit flag declarations in the collected component projection are compared; config files and defaults are not inferred.
k8s.ports.cronjob.container_argument_api.fail_when: Any captured kube-apiserver container: --anonymous-auth is declared with a value other than 'false'.
k8s.ports.cronjob.container_argument_api.not_applicable_when: When no container in the CronJob template is captured as kube-apiserver (component metadata), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); a flag omitted from the projection is UNKNOWN.

k8s.ports.cronjob.container_argument_aud.description: Flags a CronJob whose Pod template (spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec) contains a container identified as kube-apiserver whose captured command-line flags show a failing value: FAIL when --audit-log-maxage is an integer below 30. Short audit retention deletes evidence before incidents are detected. Only explicit flag declarations in the collected component projection are compared; config files and defaults are not inferred.
k8s.ports.cronjob.container_argument_aud.pass_when: Every captured kube-apiserver container: --audit-log-maxage is an integer >= 30.
k8s.ports.cronjob.container_argument_aud.fail_when: Any captured kube-apiserver container: --audit-log-maxage is an integer below 30.
k8s.ports.cronjob.container_argument_aud.not_applicable_when: When no container in the CronJob template is captured as kube-apiserver (component metadata), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results); a flag omitted from the projection is UNKNOWN.

k8s.ports.cronjob.container_argument_aud.description: Flags a CronJob whose Pod template (spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec) contains a container identified as kube-apiserver whose captured command-line flags show a failing value: FAIL when --audit-log-maxbackup is an integer below 10. Too few rotated audit files means older audit evidence is discarded quickly. Only explicit flag declarations in the collected component projection are compared; config files and defaults are not inferred.
k8s.ports.cronjob.container_argument_aud.pass_when: Every captured kube-apiserver container: --audit-log-maxbackup is an integer >= 10.
k8s.ports.cronjob.container_argument_aud.fail_when: Any captured kube-apiserver container: --audit-log-maxbackup is an integer below 10.
